items.title: ‘Once installed, there’s no getting rid of it’: what Falklands oil plans mean for its seals, whales and penguins
items.desc: While Argentina and the UK dispute sovereignty over the islands and its vast oil reserves, environmentalists fear for one of the Atlantic’s richest ecosystems From the air, the main Falkland Islands form two large, jagged shapes against the South Atlantic. East Falkland and West Falkland are surrounded by 778 smaller islands and islets east of Patagonia’s southern tip. The archipelago, a British overseas territory claimed by Argentina, is home to large colonies of albatrosses and penguins. Its waters, with those of the Patagonian shelf, provide feeding grounds for sea lions, southern elephant seals and southern right whales. Continue reading...
